subject: Applied Calculus
sourceBasis: ACADRIX MA25C01 Unit I notes: functions and graphs, limits, continuity, limits at infinity, derivatives, maxima/minima, Mean Value Theorem and graph shape.
note: Original ACADRIX exam-practice problems; not claimed official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.question: Evaluate a nontrivial limit using an appropriate algebraic or standard limiting technique and justify each transformation.
solutionPlan: Choose factoring, rationalization, standard limits or another suitable method.
Simplify without changing the limit value.

questions.question: Determine the value of a parameter that makes a piecewise-defined function continuous at a specified point, and verify continuity.
solutionPlan: Evaluate the function value at the point.
Equate the required quantities and solve for the parameter.

questions.question: Evaluate the limiting behaviour of a function as the independent variable tends to positive or negative infinity and interpret the result graphically.
solutionPlan: Identify dominant terms or standard limiting form.
Divide by the appropriate highest power when useful.

questions.question: Find the derivative of a suitable function from first principles using the difference quotient.
solutionPlan: Simplify and cancel the common factor.
Take the limit as h approaches zero.

questions.question: Differentiate a composite algebraic, trigonometric, exponential or logarithmic function using the appropriate differentiation rules.
solutionPlan: Identify product, quotient or composite structures.
Use the chain rule for nested functions.
Check the result by structure or a quick special-case test.

questions.question: Find the derivative of an implicitly defined relation and determine the slope at a specified point.
solutionPlan: Differentiate both sides with respect to x.
Apply the chain rule to y-dependent terms.

questions.question: Formulate and solve a related-rates problem by differentiating a governing relation with respect to time.
solutionPlan: Define the changing variables and their rates.
Substitute known instantaneous values and rates.
Solve for the required rate with units.

questions.question: Verify the conditions of the Mean Value Theorem for a function on a closed interval and determine the point or points guaranteed by the theorem.
solutionPlan: Check continuity on the closed interval.
Check differentiability on the open interval.
Compute the average rate of change.
Set f'(c) equal to that average rate.
Solve for all c inside the interval.

questions.question: Verify Rolle's theorem for a suitable function and determine the point at which the tangent is horizontal.
Determine the local and absolute maxima and minima of a function on a specified interval.
solutionPlan: Find critical points where f'=0 or f' is undefined.
Check endpoints for an absolute-extrema problem.
Classify critical points using the first- or second-derivative test.
State the absolute and local extrema clearly.

questions.question: Use the first derivative test to locate and classify turning points of a function and determine intervals of increase and decrease.
solutionPlan: Classify sign changes around each critical number.
State local extrema and monotonic intervals.

questions.question: Use the second derivative to classify critical points and determine concavity and possible inflection points.
solutionPlan: Use f'' at each relevant point to classify local extrema when applicable.
Check sign changes in f'' for inflection points.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of a function using domain, intercepts, asymptotic behaviour, critical points, monotonicity, concavity and inflection information.
solutionPlan: Combine the information into a labelled sketch.

questions.question: Formulate and solve a single-variable engineering optimization problem using differential calculus, including the physical interpretation of the optimum.
solutionPlan: Define the design variable and feasible domain.
Check endpoints/feasibility and classify the optimum.
Report the optimum with appropriate units and interpretation.

questions.question: Solve a complete differential-calculus problem requiring limits or continuity followed by differentiation, critical-point analysis and a graphical conclusion.
solutionPlan: Establish the required domain/continuity or limit behaviour.
Analyze monotonicity and concavity as required.
Give the final extrema or graph interpretation.

examChecklist: Check the form before evaluating a limit.
For piecewise continuity, match left limit, right limit and function value.
Use the chain rule carefully for composite functions.
For MVT/Rolle problems, verify hypotheses before solving for c.
For absolute extrema on a closed interval, compare critical points and endpoints.
Use sign charts for reliable increasing/decreasing and first-derivative classification.
For curve sketching, combine asymptotes, extrema, monotonicity, concavity and inflection points.
For engineering optimization, define the feasible domain and interpret the final result physically.
